thread:
maria: Heads up — saw a ~2.3x p99 latency jump on paged-flash variant for long-context workloads since the kernel-selector change in main (commit ab12f3c). Repro at scale: 8k seq, batch=1, throughput drops and p99 spikes.

tony: can you paste the bench command + numbers? suspect this is the selector preferring fused path for some strides.

maria: repro command I used:
```
./scripts/perf/run_attention_bench \ 
  --model=gpt-like-13b --variant=flash-paged --seq_len=8192 --batch=1 --kv_mode=paged --warmups=5 --iters=20
```
Results (avg over 3 runs):
- before (tag v2.14): p50 180ms, p95 240ms, p99 290ms
- after (main @ ab12f3c): p50 190ms, p95 520ms, p99 670ms

leah: that's pretty bad. Median unaffected much but tail doubled. Any obvious OOMs or retries?

maria: no OOMs. Logs show a kernel fallback churn where selector picks "fused_flash" for some keys and then falls back to "paged_flash" repeatedly on the same request. Found this in runtime logs:
```
[selector] seq=8192 stride=128 chosen=fused_flash
[selector] runtime_check failed: insufficient_shared_mem -> fallback_to=paged_flash
[selector] chosen=paged_flash
```
That flip-flopping correlates with higher latency and extra kernel launches.

ton y: flip-flop likely due to the new scheduling heuristic that estimates shared mem vs required workspace lazily. If estimate toggles across layers, we get double-launch. Do you have a kernel-launch profile (cuda events) showing the extra launches?

maria: yes, here's a condensed timeline (from perf traces):
```
launch #1 fused_flash  -> cudaSync -> 3.2ms
launch #2 fallback paged_flash -> cudaSync -> 12.1ms
launch #3 paged_flash (retry) -> cudaSync -> 11.8ms
```
So two extra kernel launches + synchronization overhead per affected request.

ci-bot: perf job uploaded: https://ci.internal.redwood/jobs/12345 (includes traces, pprof, and kernel logs)

leah: nice. Any differences in batch formation or KV cache hits? Could batching heuristics cause different stride patterns at runtime?

maria: good point — we saw correlated changes in batching schedule: the new batching window groups certain prefix sizes together, which increases stride from 64 -> 128 for some requests. The fused kernel has a different shared mem requirement when stride>=96 and our selector currently computes a tight threshold that sometimes underestimates. Combined this yields the occasional choose-then-fallback pattern.

tony: idea: make selector evaluate fallback checks earlier (preflight check) and mark a variant as infeasible for the whole batch rather than per-layer oscillation. Quick fix: add a per-request feasibility cache keyed by (variant, stride, seq_len). Can you try a patch locally to short-circuit fused for stride>=96 and run the bench?

maria: applied quick patch to hard-disable fused when stride>95 and reran. Results (single run): p50 188ms, p95 260ms, p99 300ms — back to baseline. Patch diff:
```
if (stride > 95) {
  mark_variant_infeasible(VARIANT_FUSED);
}
```

leah: congrats — that strongly implicates the selector threshold. But that's a blunt instrument; long term we should fix the estimator.

tony: agree. Next steps: 1) add feasibility cache to avoid per-layer re-eval 2) improve shared-mem estimator using max_workspace_for_layer() instead of heuristic 3) add unit tests that simulate stride jitter to prevent regressions. I can take (1) and (3); maria can prototype estimator changes.

maria: will start on estimator. Opening a draft PR with the quick disable as a guardrail: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/7582 — mark as hotfix for dedicated customers if CI and perf checks pass.

ci-bot: build + perf smoke queued: job 12346

tony: also add an experiment metric in console: count_selector_fallbacks per route so we can alert on sudden increases.

leah: good metric. Also please tag all affected perf traces in the incident tracker (link in the PR description) so SRE can correlate client-side retry rates.

maria: agreed. I'll attach traces and the bisect notes. If anyone wants to help with a proper estimator I have a notebook with layer workspace breakdowns (will upload). For now, rolling the guardrail to staging.

tony: thanks — really nice triage. :thumbsup:

maria: thanks team. I'll post follow-ups once estimator prototype has numbers. :eyes:
